title: Fix the source, not only the copy
statement: Put every fix into the generator or specification that made the content, not only into the stored items, because regeneration undoes fixes made only to the output.
detail: In a Grade 3 reading course, a generator's output was copied by hand into the shipped lessons, with no script or manifest linking the two, so no build step could report a drift between them (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/feedback-2026-08-06-addendum.md`, §D). A rule fixed in the generator prompt did not reach lessons already on disk, and a fix applied on disk did not survive the next regeneration, which has happened, so the course now gives every adopted rule both homes. Its content-integrity skill treats upstream generation specifications as content: a rendered lesson that quietly fixes a bad specification does not close the defect, because regeneration can bring it back (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-content-integrity/SKILL.md`). A defect repeated across a batch is the generator's, not a set of separate item faults.

evidence.quote: **The generator and the shipped lesson are not coupled by anything.**
A rule fixed in the generator prompt does not reach any lesson already on disk, and a fix applied on disk does not survive the next regen
So every adopted rule needs BOTH homes, and a verdict that names only one of them is half a fix.
Upstream generation specifications are active content authorities.
A rendered lesson that silently fixes a bad specification does not close the upstream defect because regeneration can reintroduce it.
systematic defect patterns (same defect class across a whole batch = generator prompt bug, not per-item fixes).
